content: Erythromycin is a macrolide antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It may also be prescribed to prevent certain bacterial infections. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Erythromycin should be taken orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using it to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may result in a return of the infection. If you are taking it to prevent infections, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain or cramping, and loss of appetite. Taking the medication with food may help reduce these symptoms. Rarely, erythromycin may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. diff), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Precautions: Before taking erythromycin, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin, clarithromycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Erythromycin may cause a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation), which can lead to serious (rarely fatal) irregular heartbeat. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk. This risk may be higher if you use certain drugs (e.g., diuretics) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Erythromycin may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), reducing their effectiveness. Some erythromycin products may contain sodium, which should be considered if you are on a sodium-restricted diet. Infants may be at higher risk for a serious stomach condition called infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis (IHPS). Parents should contact their physician if vomiting or irritability with feeding occurs. Drug Interactions: Erythromycin can interact with other medications, potentially altering how they work or increasing the risk of side effects. It may slow the removal of certain drugs from your body, affecting their efficacy. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Avoid co-administration with drugs such as terfenadine, cisapride, astemizole, pimozide, and certain statins (e.g., lovastatin, simvastatin), as these combinations can lead to serious side effects. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Different brands of erythromycin may have different storage requirements. Check the product packaging for specific instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not freeze the medication or store it in the bathroom. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
